title: Request-path telemetry synchronizer and anomaly bridger
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight synchronizer that links sampled tracing spans to metric/log pipelines using a stable request-path fingerprint. The goal is to reduce false-positive SLO burn-rate alerts for low-volume routes and improve anomaly fidelity for routes with sporadic traffic by enriching metrics with sampled-span context and a short-lived route alias map.
background: We've observed noisy burn-rate paging on low-cardinality SLOs where bursty traffic from background jobs or infrequent endpoints cause transient percentiles to spike. Current alert rules rely solely on metric fingerprints and do not have access to span-derived route grouping or sampling decisions. This task introduces a hook and pipeline bridge to combine sparse tracing signals with aggregated metrics so that the alerting layer can make more informed decisions (e.g., ignore single-span spikes, apply route-weighted smoothing, or escalate only when both metrics and traces indicate degradation).
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hook adds a stable route_fingerprint tag to sampled spans for all HTTP/gRPC server handlers without increasing span size > 128 bytes
A telemetry synchronizer service consumes sampled spans and emits enrichment events into the metrics pipeline within 5s of span completion
Alerting rules for route-level latency burn-rate can optionally reference the enrichment presence flag and reduce false positives by >= 40% on historical test set
Dashboards show a new request-path heatmap with synchronized metric+trace overlays and a toggle to view route alias mapping
Rolling deploy completed with no user-facing latency regression and feature behind an opt-in flag: observability.enable_route_sync
technical_notes: Design uses a stable hashing of normalized request paths (strip ids, keep route tokens) to create route_fingerprint. The tracing hook runs inside the server span creation path and writes the fingerprint as an integer tag. Sampled spans flow to the existing trace-ingest Kafka topic; a new lightweight consumer (route-sync worker) deduplicates fingerprints per minute and emits enrichment messages to metrics-ingest topic as a compact protobuf with fields: fingerprint, example_path, sample_count, top_status_codes. Enrichment TTL in pipeline is 3 minutes. For low-volume routes we apply Bayesian smoothing before computing burn-rate to avoid single-sample volatility. All components will instrument their own SLOs and include per-tenant quotas to bound cardinality.
tasks: Spec: finalize route normalization rules and hashing algorithm (PRD link below)
Implement tracing hook in server middleware (Go/Node) to add route_fingerprint tag
Build route-sync worker (consumer) with dedupe + enrichment emitter
Add enrichment joiner in metrics pipeline (Statestore enrichment stage) to attach presence and sample_count to metric series
Author new alert rule templates that reference enrichment presence and route-weighted smoothing
Create dashboards and SLO views: route heatmap, sample-backed latency percentiles, and false-positive report
Integration tests using traffic replay harness and historical incident traces
Staged rollout with feature flag and monitored canary
testing_plan: Unit tests for the normalization/hashing library; e2e replay harness where we inject historical traces and metric spikes to validate the enrichment reduces alerts; load test the route-sync worker to 10k unique fingerprints/minute; run the burn-rate retrospective analysis comparing baseline alerts to enriched-alerts over two weeks of production traffic in a shadow mode.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Deploy tracing hook to canary fleet (10% traffic) and run route-sync in shadow to verify no enrichment output changes. 3) Enable enrichment joiner in metrics pipeline in read-only mode for 24h, collect telemetry. 4) Flip enrichment into active mode for non-critical namespaces for 48h. 5) Gradually expand to all namespaces, monitor SLOs, and run postmortem metrics for 7 days.
